tracks.title: Next Edge
tracks.sub: A war room for Pi Next participants
tracks.vo: This is Next Edge, a war room for Pi Next participants.
The Pi Next prize pool is two hundred thousand US dollars. But seventy five percent of that money goes to real user engagement and retention, not to better code.
So Next Edge is a tool you come back to, not a report you read once. Start with the topic matcher: five questions about your stack, hours and assets.
The engine scores five candidate ideas against your answers. Everything is computed locally, so nothing you answer leaves your device.
Then a phased forty six day plan, from eligibility checks to final submission. Every task says why it matters and how long it takes.
Tick one off and progress saves instantly, even before you sign in.
A daily check-in builds a streak. That is the retention hook, the thing that brings people back.
And a research library where every conclusion is cross checked against official sources, each with a confidence rating.

tracks.title: A decision problem, not a coding problem
tracks.sub: Solo developers and small teams entering Pi Next
tracks.vo: This is for solo developers and small teams deciding what to build, and worried about finishing it.
And Pi is how you sign in. No new account, no email, no password. Your Pi identity is your account.
Sign in once and your progress syncs across devices, inside PiNet.

tracks.title: Pick the right topic. Then finish it.
tracks.sub: Built for Pi Next, on Pi
tracks.vo: Next Edge. Pick the right topic, then finish it. Built for Pi Next, on Pi. Thank you.
